subject: AI & Agents
title: Recurrent Networks: AI That Remembers
description: A quick win: understand Recurrent Networks: AI That Remembers.

hook.text: To understand 'it' in 'The cat sat. It purred.' you need to remember 'cat.' RNNs do that.

buildup.text: Recurrent Neural Networks pass information from one step to the next, creating a form of memory.

discovery.text: LSTMs added gates that control what to remember and what to forget at each step.

twist.text: RNNs process sequentially — slow. Transformers replaced them by processing in parallel.

climax.text: RNNs pioneered sequence modeling. Transformers inherited the crown and ran with it.

punchline.text: Remember the past. Transformers just do it faster.

quiz.question: What limitation of RNNs did transformers solve?
options: RNNs process sequentially and are slow; transformers parallelize

details.summary: Recurrent neural networks process sequences by maintaining a hidden state that carries information from previous steps. This memory mechanism lets them handle text, time series, and speech in order.
details.whyItMatters: RNNs introduced the concept of memory into neural networks, enabling AI to process sequential data. Though largely replaced by Transformers, RNN concepts remain foundational to sequence modeling.
takeaways: RNNs process inputs one step at a time, maintaining memory
Hidden states carry information from earlier in the sequence
They enabled early successes in translation and speech recognition

faq.question: What problem do recurrent networks solve?
faq.answer: Standard neural networks process each input independently. RNNs maintain a hidden state that acts as memory, letting them understand sequences where order matters — like words in a sentence or stock prices over time.

faq.question: Why have Transformers replaced RNNs?
faq.answer: RNNs process sequences one step at a time, making them slow to train on long sequences. Transformers process all positions simultaneously using attention, enabling faster training and better long-range understanding.
